candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory source control and visitor screening
candidate.educational_objective: Apply respiratory-infection screening and source-control measures to symptomatic visitors in outpatient oncology settings before they enter patient-care areas.

options.A: Provide a facemask and ask the symptomatic family member not to enter patient-care areas, encouraging the person to wait outside or defer the visit.
options.B: Allow the family member into the treatment area without additional measures because only confirmed respiratory infections require precautions.
options.C: Permit entry as long as the family member avoids touching the client and remains at least one chair away from other people.
options.D: Delay screening until the family member develops fever because cough and congestion alone are not sufficient reasons for respiratory precautions.

candidate.rationale: CDC guidance for outpatient oncology settings applies respiratory-hygiene measures to patients, family members, caregivers, and visitors with respiratory symptoms such as cough or congestion. Symptomatic persons should be provided a facemask as appropriate, and accompanying persons with respiratory symptoms should not enter patient-care areas and should be encouraged to wait outside the facility. Precautions do not require a confirmed diagnosis or fever before action is taken.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC applies respiratory-hygiene and source-control measures to symptomatic visitors and accompanying persons; outpatient oncology guidance states that accompanying persons with respiratory symptoms should not enter patient-care areas and should be encouraged to wait outside, with facemasks provided to symptomatic persons as appropriate.

candidate.stem: A family member accompanies a client to an outpatient oncology clinic and reports a new cough and nasal congestion. Which action by clinic staff is appropriate?
